## Decision record: what the comparison face promises, and what its receipts look like

::: {.callout .callout-note}
**Decision.** CS-19 is a witness, not a specification: it freezes what the
exported `ms_compare()` generic and its `MsComparison` container actually
adjudicate over planted dictionary-comparison calls, so future drift speaks
immediately. It commits only machine-stable facts: the error CLASS always,
and the message CLAUSES verbatim -- every one of them. The face runs a
three-protocol kernel over share-normalized columns and a null Monte Carlo
family; its verdicts are pure functions of the planted dictionaries and the
recorded seed. But the ACCEPTED arms return real similarity matrices, so
under the D11 cross-platform posture no float payload can ride a
byte-committed column: the accepted renders commit a DISCRETE similarity
GLYPH (`1`/`0`, NA when the entry is NA) at a 1e-9 threshold, seven orders
above the observed kernel error (~1e-16), instead of the numbers themselves.
Integer, label, logical, class and clause bytes are byte-committed; floats
are censused finite/in-domain only. The lane also found, and committed, the
face's two rejection LAYERS: the S7 property-type check fires ahead of the
custom comparison validator, so the class token tells the reader which gate
spoke.
:::

### The face

`ms_compare(estimated, reference, metric = "cosine", protocol = ...)` is the
exported S7 generic (`R/ms-compare.R:468`) that scores an estimated
dictionary against a reference one: it computes pairwise similarity
matrices column-wise over a shared channel space, then runs up to three
matching protocols (Hungarian, Islam, Jiang) and two null families, and
assembles everything into an `MsComparison` container
(`R/classes-compare.R:114`). The metric roster is frozen
(`cosine`, `correlation`, `jsd`, `hellinger` -- the last as `sqrt(JSD)`),
the protocol roster is frozen (`hungarian`, `islam`, `jiang`), and every
null draw rides the recorded `seed` (PCG64 layout v1). CS-19 fires 54
observation arms at it plus eight boundary-pair rows: 23 law arms, 13
acceptance specs, 10 precedence discriminators, 8 degenerate rows (4
pairs), 12 scalars. The committed lane replays every arm live: the law file
adjudicates 263 expectations across 10 units (0 failed, 0 errors, 0
skipped, 0 warnings) and the runner rails every row against the frozen
block before any witness byte is written.

### The two rejection layers -- and why the class token matters

The face refuses a malformed argument at one of two gates, and the witness
commits the split as measured. The **custom validator**
`msuiter_validate_comparison()` speaks every value/shape violation:
metrics that are not a named non-empty list of numeric matrices, a
`hungarian` slot that is not a data frame, a `jiang` or `null` slot that is
not a named list -- all `msuiter_error_comparison`. The **S7 property-type
check** runs BEFORE it: a bare `ms_compare()` result whose `@metrics` or
`@meta` is the wrong *type* never reaches the custom validator at all, and
the class token is the base `simpleError` carrying the S7 diagnostic
(`<msuiter::MsComparison> object properties are invalid: | - @metrics must
be <list>, not <double>`). The `container-classes` scalar speaks both
layers at once -- the value is literally
`msuiter_error_comparison,simpleError` -- and the U8 unit re-derives it, so
a drift that collapsed the two gates into one reddens the lane. Everything
upstream of the container -- the estimated/reference matrices, the channel
count, the thresholds, the seed, the Jiang exposures -- refuses earlier, as
`msuiter_error_input` (thirteen arms: shape, value, channel, floor,
thresholds, seed, Jiang) or `msuiter_error_option` (the two frozen roster
arms, which also re-fire as precedence discriminators).

### The laws the face demonstrates

- **The matrix laws.** A non-numeric or non-matrix `estimated`/`reference`
  refuses as `msuiter_error_input` -- "estimated must be a numeric matrix"
  / "reference must be a numeric matrix" -- naming the received class
  ("received: numeric") and the `m x k` remedy; a matrix with an NA,
  non-finite or negative entry refuses -- "estimated must be finite and
  non-negative" -- counting the offending entries against the
  share-vector bullet.
- **The shared-space law.** Dictionaries whose channel counts differ refuse
  -- "estimated and reference must share the channel count" -- naming both
  row counts and the project-onto-one-space remedy; and a single-channel
  comparison refuses at the floor -- "ms_compare needs at least 2 channels"
  -- because the null faces and the metrics are degenerate at `m = 1`.
- **The frozen-roster laws.** An unknown metric or protocol refuses as
  `msuiter_error_option` -- "metric must be among the frozen names" /
  "protocol must be among the frozen names" -- naming the unknown value and
  the legal roster it was measured against.
- **The sweep and seed laws.** A thresholds vector that is empty,
  non-numeric, NA-bearing or outside `(0, 1)` refuses -- "thresholds must be
  non-empty numeric in (0, 1)"; a seed that is not a single non-negative
  finite number refuses -- "seed must be a single non-negative finite
  number" (the audit #74 P2 seed gate, which `ms_compare` had been the one
  FFI-facing face to lack).
- **The Jiang laws.** The Jiang protocol needs both exposure matrices
  ("the Jiang protocol needs both exposure matrices", naming which are
  missing), cell-aligned exposures ("the Jiang protocol needs cell-aligned
  exposure matrices (the true dictionary fitted)", naming both signature
  counts), a catalog with the shared channel count, and a `k x n` exposure
  shape -- plus, for the reconstruction flag, a `signatures_est` that is
  `m x k_est`.
- **The container laws.** The custom validator's five slots each carry
  their own clause and remedy bullet ("pass the metrics list returned by
  ms_compare()" / "pass the slots assembled by ms_compare()"); two of them
  are outranked in practice by the S7 property check, which is what the
  K7/K8 arms witness.
- **Precedence.** Ten discriminators, each with its fires anchor pinned
  PRESENT and its anti anchor pinned ABSENT in the same live message --
  signature-shape before the value law, the channel law before the metric
  option law, the metric option law before the protocol option law and
  before the thresholds law.
- **The acceptance specs.** The canonical render commits its full identity
  line (`msuiter::MsComparison|cosine,p_null,q_bh|3x4|6|hungarian|U-M4-01-v1|<glyph>|signature`)
  -- the metric roster, the `k_est x k_ref` shape, the channel count, the
  protocol, the frozen `protocol_version`, the discrete similarity glyph
  and the null hull. Combining protocols joins the names
  (`hungarian+islam`, `hungarian+islam+jiang`); the Jiang arm commits the
  square `3x3` shape and the `signature+catalog` hull; a singular
  correlation column commits the all-NA glyph; `jsd` and `hellinger`
  commit the all-zero glyph; replaying the committed spec through
  `ms_compare()` reproduces it byte-for-byte (the replay-identity spec
  welds two renders with `==`).

The 54-row class census (`msuiter_error_input=23`,
`s7:msuiter::MsComparison=15`, `msuiter_error_option=7`,
`msuiter_error_comparison=6`, `simpleError=2`, `s7:character=1`, over the

witnesses byte-reproduce on consecutive runner invocations, the plant and
spec corpora hash identically under BOTH governed SHA-256 kernels
(`.ms_fit_sha256` and digest), the RNG-purity rails read `FALSE` before and
after, and the lane never calls the benchmark driver, the declined
calibration family, the registry face or any validator internal (banned
words, grepped over the runner source).

### The single-source build, and the audit that became the minter

Both hosts -- law file and runner -- carry one byte-identical frozen block
and one byte-identical shared code block, each injected from a single
source between BEGIN/END markers; the splice rail demands the exact marker
counts and compares the two regions across the files byte for byte. The
minter IS the audit: every one of the 54 roster arms is re-fired LIVE
through the face against the audited probe ledger; each of the 10
precedence-path arms carries an explicit decision-record path whose
FIRES/ANTI alignment is asserted order-invariantly; every scalar is
re-fireable and re-fired; and a final RE-AUDIT re-sources the EMITTED block
into a cleared namespace and re-compares every committed literal against
the ledger -- so emitter drift, chunking drift and quoting drift all die at
mint time, not at read time. The committed clause bytes in this page are
read from the committed witnesses, never re-typed from plan.

### What the lane-building itself caught (the honest section)

The live replay killed two would-be-innocent readings before one witness
byte was trusted. First, the probe that was supposed to prove single-source
byte-identity scanned the LAW FILE for the marker strings -- but the law
file's U1 unit *quotes* each marker inside its own `.region()` literal, so
the scan counted the quotation as a second occurrence and reported a splice
violation that did not exist. The governing fact is that `.region()` reads
the RUNNER source, where each marker occurs exactly once; the probe was
corrected to scan the runner, and the FROZEN and SHARED regions then
compared byte-identical. Second, the `container-classes` scalar was first
drafted as a single class token. It is not: constructing an `MsComparison`
with a wrong-typed `@metrics` or `@meta` is stopped by the S7 property
check, not by the custom validator, so the container speaks TWO classes and
the witness commits both. Both findings are why the lane commits the
rejection LAYER, not just the rejection reason.

### Provenance

The frozen block and the shared code block in both hosts are minted
mechanically from the audited probe ledger (audit green: 54 arms byte-exact
on live re-fire, 8 degen rows, 10/10 fires-and-anti anchors, 12 scalars
re-fired); neither is ever hand-edited in place. The plants' canonical
texts hash to the committed dual-kernel checksum
(`plant_sha256=657baf56c41c183e...`, `spec_sha256=fae8b605af620e7c...`);
reifying the lane reproduces every witness byte for byte. Differentiation
from CS-18 (the converter face): CS-18 adjudicated an option resolver that
runs twice under two argument names; CS-19 adjudicates a three-protocol
similarity kernel whose accepted arms return real similarity matrices AND
whose refusals split across two gates -- the first witness class in the
series that commits a rejection LAYER (which gate spoke) alongside a
rejection REASON, and the first whose discretionary numeric output rides a
discrete glyph over a squared JSD face rather than a column-sum.

### Gate forensics

The scenarios leg for this lane (the eighteenth) was render-verified before
the full local burn. The T0 seal moved 627 -> 628 with the generator's
refusal witnessed verbatim (the DEFECT line naming 628 against the sealed
627, run against a doctored budget) before the deliberate re-seal, per the
budget law; the reified manifest carries the new law file on the T0 tier,
byte-deterministic on re-mint.
